require 'sinatra'
require 'json'
require 'openssl'
require 'base64'
require 'securerandom'
require 'redis'
require 'rack/utils'

module CryptoVault
  class KeyDerivation
    ITERATIONS = 100_000
    KEY_LENGTH = 32
    HASH_ALGO = 'sha256'

    def self.derive(master_secret, context)
      OpenSSL::KDF.pbkdf2_hmac(
        master_secret,
        salt: context,
        iterations: ITERATIONS,
        length: KEY_LENGTH,
        hash: HASH_ALGO
      )
    end
  end

  class EncryptionService
    CIPHER_ALGO = 'aes-256-gcm'
    NONCE_LENGTH = 12

    def initialize(master_key)
      @master_key = master_key
    end

    def encrypt(plaintext, purpose)
      derived_key = derive_purpose_key(purpose)
      cipher = OpenSSL::Cipher.new(CIPHER_ALGO)
      cipher.encrypt
      cipher.key = derived_key
      nonce = generate_nonce(purpose)
      cipher.iv = nonce
      cipher.auth_data = purpose.to_s

      ciphertext = cipher.update(plaintext) + cipher.final
      tag = cipher.auth_tag

      Base64.strict_encode64(nonce + tag + ciphertext)
    end

    def decrypt(encoded_data, purpose)
      raw = Base64.strict_decode64(encoded_data)
      nonce = raw[0, NONCE_LENGTH]
      tag = raw[NONCE_LENGTH, 16]
      ciphertext = raw[NONCE_LENGTH + 16..]

      derived_key = derive_purpose_key(purpose)
      cipher = OpenSSL::Cipher.new(CIPHER_ALGO)
      cipher.decrypt
      cipher.key = derived_key
      cipher.iv = nonce
      cipher.auth_tag = tag
      cipher.auth_data = purpose.to_s

      cipher.update(ciphertext) + cipher.final
    end

    private

    def derive_purpose_key(purpose)
      KeyDerivation.derive(@master_key, purpose_to_context(purpose))
    end

    def purpose_to_context(purpose)
      # Context derivation uses purpose name for domain separation
      "mobile-api-v1:#{purpose}"
    end

    def generate_nonce(purpose)
      # Random nonce generation for each encryption operation
      SecureRandom.random_bytes(NONCE_LENGTH)
    end
  end

  class SessionStore
    def initialize(redis_url, master_key)
      @redis = Redis.new(url: redis_url)
      @crypto = EncryptionService.new(master_key)
    end

    def store_session(user_id, session_data)
      encrypted = @crypto.encrypt(
        JSON.generate(session_data),
        "session:#{user_id}"
      )
      @redis.setex("sess:#{user_id}", 3600, encrypted)
    end

    def retrieve_session(user_id)
      encrypted = @redis.get("sess:#{user_id}")
      return nil unless encrypted

      decrypted = @crypto.decrypt(encrypted, "session:#{user_id}")
      JSON.parse(decrypted)
    end
  end

  class TokenStore
    def initialize(redis_url, master_key)
      @redis = Redis.new(url: redis_url)
      @crypto = EncryptionService.new(master_key)
    end

    def issue_refresh_token(user_id, device_id)
      token_data = {
        user_id: user_id,
        device_id: device_id,
        issued_at: Time.now.to_i,
        jti: SecureRandom.hex(16)
      }

      encrypted = @crypto.encrypt(
        JSON.generate(token_data),
        "refresh:#{user_id}"
      )
      @redis.setex("token:#{user_id}:#{device_id}", 86400, encrypted)
      encrypted
    end

    def validate_refresh_token(user_id, device_id, token)
      stored = @redis.get("token:#{user_id}:#{device_id}")
      return nil unless stored
      return nil unless token.is_a?(String)
      # Constant-time comparison to avoid timing side channels on the secret token
      return nil unless Rack::Utils.secure_compare(stored, token)

      decrypted = @crypto.decrypt(token, "refresh:#{user_id}")
      JSON.parse(decrypted)
    rescue OpenSSL::Cipher::CipherError, JSON::ParserError
      nil
    end
  end
end

# Application setup
MASTER_KEY = ENV.fetch('VAULT_MASTER_KEY')
REDIS_URL = ENV.fetch('REDIS_URL', 'redis://localhost:6379')

session_store = CryptoVault::SessionStore.new(REDIS_URL, MASTER_KEY)
token_store = CryptoVault::TokenStore.new(REDIS_URL, MASTER_KEY)

before do
  content_type :json
end

post '/api/v1/auth/login' do
  body = JSON.parse(request.body.read)
  user_id = body['user_id']
  device_id = body['device_id']

  # Authentication logic omitted for brevity
  session_data = { user_id: user_id, role: 'user', login_time: Time.now.to_i }
  session_store.store_session(user_id, session_data)

  refresh_token = token_store.issue_refresh_token(user_id, device_id)

  { status: 'ok', refresh_token: refresh_token }.to_json
end

post '/api/v1/auth/refresh' do
  body = JSON.parse(request.body.read)
  user_id = body['user_id']
  device_id = body['device_id']
  token = body['refresh_token']

  token_data = token_store.validate_refresh_token(user_id, device_id, token)
  halt 401, { error: 'invalid_token' }.to_json unless token_data

  new_token = token_store.issue_refresh_token(user_id, device_id)
  { status: 'ok', refresh_token: new_token }.to_json
end

get '/api/v1/user/:id/profile' do
  user_id = params[:id]

  # Enforce access control: caller must present a valid refresh token bound to
  # this user/device before their session profile is returned. This prevents
  # an unauthenticated IDOR where any user's profile could be read by ID alone.
  device_id = params[:device_id] || request.env['HTTP_X_DEVICE_ID']
  token = request.env['HTTP_AUTHORIZATION']&.sub(/\ABearer\s+/i, '')

  halt 401, { error: 'unauthorized' }.to_json if device_id.nil? || token.nil?

  unless token_store.validate_refresh_token(user_id, device_id, token)
    halt 401, { error: 'unauthorized' }.to_json
  end

  session = session_store.retrieve_session(user_id)
  halt 401, { error: 'no_session' }.to_json unless session

  { status: 'ok', profile: session }.to_json
end
